QuestionStmt.S: The statement pattern $[ (p \to q) \land \sim q ] \to r$ is a tautology when $r$ is equivalent to

Solution.S:
The truth table for the given pattern is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
p & q & r & p \to q & \sim q & (p \to q) \land \sim q \\
\hline
T & T & T & T & F & F \\
T & T & F & T & F & F \\
T & F & T & F & T & F \\
T & F & F & F & T & F \\
F & T & T & T & F & F \\
F & T & F & T & F & F \\
F & F & T & T & T & T \\
F & F & F & T & T & T \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

For $[ (p \to q) \land \sim q ] \to r$ to be a tautology, whenever the antecedent $(p \to q) \land \sim q$ is true, $r$ must be true. From the table, the antecedent is true only when $p = F$ and $q = F$. In that case, $r$ must be true. Among the options, $\sim q$ is true exactly when $q = F$. Hence $r \equiv \sim q$.

Thus the correct answer is Option D: $\sim q$.
